top_choice_rationale: P004 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) rewards the separable originating steps of modern monetary macroeconomics: time-dependent pricing, staggered contracts with policy-rule analysis, and the welfare-based synthesis. It has decades of testing through 2008 and the 2021-23 inflation, and earlier macro prizes on expectations and credibility did not cover it. Its weakness is attribution, because a three-name cut leaves out Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler. I judge that cut to be a defensible originators-versus-developers distinction, though not a certain one, and I would word the citation around nominal rigidities, contract setting and rules rather than Calvo pricing as literally true. I rank P002 (Kiyotaki-Moore) next because its attribution is cleanest and its mechanism is mature. P003 follows on framework, maturity and concentrated credit, with a weaker identification record. P001 is ahead of no award because its measurement and exposure designs are checkable and durable, but I rank it fourth because its core results are recent and the causal place-effect claims are still contested. A prize in any of P001 to P004 is better than no award.
recusal_note: No credited laureate on P001-P004 appears as a co-author or institutional connection in my profile. I am a long-time co-author of committee members John Hassler and Timo Boppart, and of Giovanni Violante, who is not on the slate. My capital-skill complementarity work is adjacent to B024, which is not on the slate. I disclose these connections without adjudicating them, and I do not treat agreement with co-authors as independent evidence.
